How it works

BraceletESP32-S3
Message brokerMosquitto · MQTT
devices/{id}/measurements
Backend serverSpring Boot
AI serverFastAPI · Python
DatabasePostgreSQL
Mobile clientReact Native · Expo

The bracelet reads heart rate, SpO₂ and motion.

Every second it publishes a reading over MQTT.

Spring Boot receives it and checks the device.

Readings go to PostgreSQL. Flyway builds the schema.

The AI model reads 75 motion samples and returns activity and fall risk.

The app gets fresh data over a secure REST API.

Setup: the app sends Wi-Fi details over Bluetooth.

One loop. Every second.

ESP32-S3 is the main control unit.

The heart sensor reads pulse and SpO₂ from the skin.

The accelerometer and gyroscope feel every move and fall.

Live values on the bracelet’s own display.

Every second, over MQTT to the server.

On a fall, the LED blinks and the buzzer sounds.
